card.name: Sorsornet
card.era: Traditional mask dance; entered national-ballet repertory 20th century
card.tagline: Baga mask rhythm and youth-initiation dance of coastal Guinea
card.profile: Sorsornet (Sorsone) is a rhythm and mask dance of the Baga people of the Boke region of coastal (western) Guinea (Tontinkan; Mande Drum and Dance). The Sorsornet mask was regarded as a bringer of good luck and almost a deity; when present in the village the rhythm is played and the mask moves through it. Associated with youth initiation and protection, the accompanying song is traditionally sung by young girls in the moonlight to thank their mothers (Tontinkan). Now men and women dance it widely at celebrations.
card.insight: Art historian Frederick Lamp's fieldwork (Art of the Baga, Museum for African Art, 1996) documents Sorsone as a Baga Sitemu masquerade with a tall raffia dress often surmounted by a horned female-bust headdress (mandebala.net).
card.image_significance: From sacred mask to women's moonlight dance. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Boke (Baga), Guinea.
